subject: Close timeline & first-response latency acceptance for EchoHealth pilot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@echohealth.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@echohealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Close timeline & first-response latency acceptance for EchoHealth pilot

Hi Maya + Jordan —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our mutual action discussion, I’m attaching the performance acceptance plan we’ll use as the gating criteria for pilot close. The two items you flagged in the call were: (1) first-response latency (time-to-first-token for streaming chat) targets and (2) steady-state concurrency under the clinical ingestion workload.

High level plan (attachments: echohealth_map_performance_plan.pdf):
- Run 3 test passes across the next two weeks: baseline, tuning, verification.
- Metrics we’ll validate: first-token latency (p50/p95/p99), streaming tail latency (p50/p95/p99 for subsequent tokens), throughput (requests/sec), and stable concurrency (clients * messages/min).
- Acceptance gates: p95 first-token <= 250ms; p99 first-token <= 450ms; concurrency sustain at 120 concurrent chat sessions with <10% p95 degradation.
- Data & instrumentation: we’ll use request-level tracing and per-token timestamps; Redwood will provide CSV of raw samples and summarized charts.

Can you confirm the two gate numbers above (p95/p99) or propose alternate thresholds? Also confirm target close date — you mentioned wanting contractual signoff by Apr 16 in the call.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm targets and the Apr 16 close target by EOD tomorrow.
2) Redwood will schedule the baseline run Apr 5–6, tuning pass Apr 8–9, verification Apr 11–12.
3) After verification we’ll deliver the results CSV and a short exec summary for signoff.

Attachment: echohealth_map_performance_plan.pdf (4 pages) — includes test harness, sample prompts, and instrumentation guide.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0187

From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@echohealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@echohealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline & first-response latency acceptance for EchoHealth pilot

Sean —

Thanks for the write-up and the plan. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- The p95/p99 thresholds you listed look reasonable as a starting point, but for our clinical triage flow we’d prefer p95 first-token <= 200ms if achievable. Is that realistic for the baseline run or only after tuning?
- For concurrency: 120 concurrent sessions is a good target. Please show the degradation curve (p95 as concurrency increases in 10-session steps) so we can evaluate the failure modes.
- Close date: Apr 16 is what we had in mind; we'd like the verification artifacts by Apr 13 if possible so our security and procurement teams can run internal checks before the 16th.

If you can aim to deliver verification results on Apr 12 (as you suggested) but push the artifacts to us by Apr 13, that would be ideal. We can be available for a brief review meeting Apr 14.

Thanks —
Maya Rao
Director, Digital Products
EchoHealth
maya.rao@echohealth.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline & first-response latency acceptance for EchoHealth pilot (internal runbook)

Quick internal note / runbook for the baseline:

- Harness: use streaming harness v2.3 (Mar 2027) with the EchoHealth prompt set (attached in Google doc). Warm-up: 120s at 20 qps to populate KV cache.
- Baseline config: model = open-7b-q4 (Redwood-verified), batch target 32 tok/request, max_seq 1024, no quant-session cache.
- Tuning pass: enable prefix caching + dynamic batching; try batch sizes 16/32/64 and measure p50/p95/p99 first-token.
- Concurrency sweep: 0–160 in +10 steps. Record p50/p95/p99 for first-token and streaming token latencies (token 2..50).
- Failure criteria: if p95 first-token increases by >20% at 120 concurrent vs 40 concurrent, mark as regression and run backoff policy tests.

I’ll own running the baseline on Apr 6 and the tuning passes Apr 8–9. Marissa — can you schedule the verification run Apr 11–12 and prepare the CSV export format we discussed?

Vanessa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@echohealth.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@echohealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline & first-response latency acceptance for EchoHealth pilot — verification results

Hi Maya + Jordan —

We completed verification on Apr 12 and attached the results CSV (echohealth_streaming_results.csv) plus a two-page exec summary in the Hub doc link. Summary highlights below; full data attached.

Quick verdict: verification PASS for your target close on Apr 16, with one recommended tuning change (enable longer prefix cache TTL) to tighten the p99 tail under heavy concurrency.

Key numbers (verification run, median of 3 passes):
- First-response (time-to-first-token) — p50: 82 ms; p95: 192 ms; p99: 402 ms.
- Streaming subsequent-token tail (tokens 2–50) — p50: 6 ms/token; p95: 28 ms/token; p99: 72 ms/token.
- Throughput: sustained 520 requests/sec at 120 concurrent sessions (steady-state).
- Concurrency sweep note: p95 first-token increases from 175 ms at 40 concurrent to 192 ms at 120 concurrent (≈9.7% increase) — within the <10% degradation acceptance gate.

Attachments: echohealth_streaming_results.csv (rows: run_id,timestamp,request_id,first_token_ms,token_index,token_ms,concurrency,config_tag)

Recommended tuning: set prefix cache TTL to 90s (current plan used 30s) — this reduces p99 first-token by ~8% on our tuning pass. We can apply that change before you move to production if you want the tighter tail.

Next steps you requested:
- We’ll push the CSV + exec summary to your procurement/security teams by Apr 13 (HubSpot link below).
- If Proc/Sec have questions we can do a 30-min walkthrough Apr 14.
- Assuming signoff, Redwood will issue the standard pilot completion form for contractual close on Apr 16.

Hub doc (exec summary + charts): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcEchoHealth-MAP
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/echohealth

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the charts.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
